title: The 8-gate list is a third copy of the workflow contract, anchored by comments only — no drift guard
evidence:
# The gate list mirrors .github/workflows/ci.yml step-for-step — the workflow
# is the spec; never edit one without the other. Same order, same failure
# semantics (stop on first failure), same per-gate names in the summary.
...
GATES=(
  "Purity + grep gates (ODN-1)|tools/lint.sh"
  "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|odin test core"
  "Game builds (app.bin compiles + links)|odin build app -out:app.bin"
detail: The workflow has grown a gate with nearly every story (1.2, W1, preview-check, 5.7); with GH billing-blocked the local suite is now the only verification. A new ci.yml step not mirrored in GATES silently weakens it.
recommended_fix: Keep the anchored header, and add an audit note to the workflow's own header comment (or a lint gate) that ci-local.sh GATES + the README table must mirror any new step.

title: .dockerignore is a strict subset of .gitignore's artifact set — several gitignored artifact paths are not excluded
evidence:
.dockerignore:
bin
tools/raylib-sw
goldens/_reports
app*.bin
app-win.exe
*.dSYM
.env
_bmad-output/**/.build

.gitignore (not mirrored):
export/
*.pck
*.apk
*.aab
*.ipa
*.dmg
*.zip
.godot/
game/tests/captures/
detail: Verified no current gate produces these paths (outputs are only bin/, tools/raylib-sw/, goldens/_reports/, app*.bin, app-win.exe, *.dSYM), so no live hole; but the header claims the container 'never sees a host build' — the guarantee rests on the two lists never drifting.
recommended_fix: Mirror the missing gitignored artifact patterns (export/, *.dmg, *.zip, *.pck, *.apk, *.aab, *.ipa, *.blend1, .godot/, game/tests/captures/) in .dockerignore, or qualify the blanket isolation claim.

title: Host-side `--in-container --windows-cross` probes the HOST toolchain while printing in-container messaging
evidence:
# (probes the LOCAL toolchain; use --in-container for the container's)
...
      echo "   ✅ windows_amd64 cross-build succeeded → app-win.exe (in-container; the --rm container discards it)"
...
if [ "$WIN_CROSS" -eq 1 ]; then
  run_windows_cross
  exit $?
fi

if [ "$IN_CONTAINER" -eq 1 ]; then
  run_gates "$([ "$FAST" -eq 1 ] && echo 2 || echo 8)"
detail: IN_CONTAINER only changes the success message; run_windows_cross never touches docker, and the WIN_CROSS branch dispatches before the IN_CONTAINER branch. The documented flag pair mislabels host-toolchain results as container results — the two toolchains can differ (linux lld cross-link).
recommended_fix: Set a marker env in the image CMD and refuse --in-container outside a container; or make host-side --windows-cross --in-container exec the probe via docker run instead of running it directly.
